summary: An inline message about the state of a page or a section: a failed publish, a pending review, a sync in progress. It stays until the situation changes or the user dismisses it.
whenToUse: A condition that affects what the user is doing here: a failed build, a protected branch, contrast warnings.
Tone follows meaning: danger for failed or blocked, warning for needs attention, success for a finished task that changed this page, info for context, neutral when there is no judgement.
Inside a form or card, above the content it is about.

actionsPlacement inline for one short message and one action, like a banner saying which change you are viewing with Back to latest at the end of the line. It wraps under the text on a phone. Keep below for a title plus a longer description.
whenNotToUse: Confirming an action the user just took (Copied, Saved): use a Toast.
An error on one field: use the Field error under that control.
A decision the user must make before continuing: use an AlertDialog.

dos.title: Title says what happened, description says what to do
dos.text: Users scan the bold line and read on only when they need to act.

children: The token build found 2 broken aliases. Fix them and publish again.

dos.title: Give the way out as an action
dos.text: A button next to the problem saves a search through the page.

children: Token changes need a design owner and a tech owner.

donts.title: Stacking several alerts
donts.text: Three alerts in a row read as noise. Merge them, or keep the most severe and link to the rest.

donts.title: Danger for something that is not broken
donts.text: Red trains people to ignore red. Use info or warning when nothing failed.

accessibility: Alerts that appear after load are announced: danger and warning with role="alert" (interrupts), the others with role="status" (polite).
Alerts present when the page loads should use announce="off": a live region on load is either ignored or read twice.
Every tone has its own icon and the text carries the meaning, so color is never the only signal (WCAG 1.4.1).
The dismiss button is a named IconButton (dismissLabel, default "Dismiss"). Move focus to a sensible place after dismissing if the alert had focus.
Feedback text and icon colors are checked against their tinted backgrounds in both themes.
contentGuidelines: Title: what happened, in a few words, no period: "Publish failed".
Description: why, and what to do next, in one or two sentences.
Name objects and numbers: "3 tokens fail contrast", not "Some issues were found".
No apology, no blame, no exclamation marks.
